minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  October 7, 2013

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Reardon at 5:01 p.m., on October 7, 2013, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on October 2, 2013, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Leckness
  Council Member Schlicht
  Council Member Ury
  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley (present until 5:26 p.m. only)
  Mayor Reardon

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Ury

INVOCATION: Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

CONSIDERATION OF ADDED AGENDA ITEM 1

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that staff would like to add two items to the agenda
pursuant to California Government Code Section 54954.2(b2). Adding items to the agenda
requires a 2/3rd vote and two findings: (1) that there is a need to take immediate action, and (2)
that the matter arose subsequent to the posting of the City Council agenda. The first matter
City Council Minutes  1  October 7, 2013
 relates to an Orange County Fire Authority Special Board Meeting that is occurring at 6:00 p.m.
tonight. The Council may want to give direction to its OCFA representative, Mayor Pro Tem
Kelley, so she can take the Council's comments to the OCFA meeting this evening. The issue
being considered by OCFA relates to a County Board of Supervisors action that is scheduled to
be taken tomorrow morning so the Council cannot delay discussion of this matter.

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ury, to declare a need
subsequent to the positing of the agenda to address the proposed Orange County Board of
Supervisors consideration of authority to award ambulance contracts and the Orange County Fire
Authority's process for Requests for Proposals.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon and Ury
NOES:  Schlicht
ABSENT:  None

ADDED AGENDA ITEM 1

Consideration of the Proposed Orange County Board of Supervisors Consideration of
Authority to Award Ambulance Contracts and the Orange County Fire Authority’s
Process for Requests for Proposals for Ambulance Services

Mayor Reardon read a letter that she signed this afternoon. The letter is addressed to Orange
County Supervisor Patricia Bates and requests that the Board of Supervisors delay any action on
agenda item S16A which recommends rescission of County Resolution 04-120 regarding
ambulance service providers. By sending the letter, the City is requesting that the matter be
delayed so that Mission Viejo has time to provide input to the Board regarding this issue.

City Manager Wilberg provided a brief summary of the implications that the Board's proposed
action might have. He asked the Council to consider sending the Mayor's letter to the Board of
Supervisor and to send copies with Mayor Pro Tem Kelly to the OCFA special meeting tonight.

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ury, to authorize staff to
send the letter, signed by Mayor Reardon, to the County Board of Supervisors requesting that
they delay action on Board of Supervisors Agenda Item S16A.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon and Ury
NOES:  Schlicht
ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  2  October 7, 2013
 CONSIDERATION OF ADDED AGENDA ITEM 2

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that staff would like to add another item to the agenda
pursuant to California Government Code Section 54954.2(b2). There is a need to take
immediate action as Assemblywoman Harkey is in the audience tonight and the matter arose
after posting of the Agenda.

Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to approve the
addition of an item to the agenda for Assemblywoman Diane Harkey's presentation of a
resolution recognizing the City's anniversaries.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley departed the meeting at 5:26 p.m. to attend the Special Meeting of the
OCFA Board of Directors.

ADDED AGENDA ITEM 2

Presentation of a Resolution by Assemblywoman Diane Harkey in Recognition of the City’s
50th Year as a Community and 25th Year as a City

Assemblywoman Diane Harkey presented the City with the resolution.

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Legal Counsel: Anticipated Litigation Initiation of Litigation
  Pursuant to Subdivision (c) of Section 54956.9: One Potential Case.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:34 p.m., Mayor Reardon recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:04 p.m. with four City Council Members present. Mayor Pro Tem
Kelley left the Council Meeting at 5:26 p.m. in order to attend a special meeting of the OCFA
Board of Directors.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council received an update and gave direction to
staff but there was no reportable action from Closed Session.

City Council Minutes  3  October 7, 2013
 ANNOUNCEMENT REGARDING ITEMS ADDED TO THE AGENDA SUBSEQUENT
TO THE POSTING OF THE AGENDA

Mr. Curley provided an outline of the Council’s action, prior to the Closed Session, to approve a
letter to the County Board of Supervisors requesting that the Board delay decision on an October
8 agenda item regarding the award of ambulance service contracts.

Council Member Schlicht announced that she voted no because she believes that the Board of
Supervisors has the unique position to move forward on the matter.

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Recognition as "Employer of the Year" by the California Disabilities Services
  Association

  Mayor Reardon received the award from Vocational Visions Executive Director Joan
  Mckinney and Community Employment Manager Roland F. Fernandez.

P2. Proclaim October 6 through October 12, 2013 To Be Fire Prevention Week

  Mayor Reardon presented the proclamation to OCFA Battalion Chief Tim Perkins.

P3. 2013 Walk Against Drugs

  The City Council received a presentation on the 2013 Walk Against Drugs from
  Community Outreach Coordinator Tammy Descoteaux.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Larry Gilbert, M.V.: presented the City Council with a copy of a column that he wrote for the
Community Common Sense newspaper in which he expressed his opposition to the expenditure
of $1.3 million of developer park fees for a special needs playground at Pavion Park.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Leckness, to approve the
Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

City Council Minutes  4  October 7, 2013
 AYES:  Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  Kelley

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and
  further reading waived.

7.  Year-End Financial Report for the City of Mission Viejo for the Twelve Months
  Ended June 30, 2013

  Received and filed.

8.  Semi-Annual Financial Report for the Community Development Financing Authority
  - For the Year Ended June 30, 2013

  Received and filed.

9.  City Treasurer’s Annual Report for Fiscal Year 2012-2013 and Annual Review of
  City’s Investment Policy

  (1) Received and filed the City Treasurer's Annual Report for fiscal year 2012-13; (2)
  adopted Resolution 13-54 Approving the City's Investment Policy for FY 2013-14; and (3)
  set the Benchmark Index for FY 2013-14 to be a Government Securities Index comprised
  of 60% three-month Treasury Bills; 25% Treasury and Agency securities with maturities
  greater than one year and up to three years; and 15% Treasury and Agency securities with
  maturities greater than three years and up to five years.

10. Community Development Financing Authority (CDFA) Treasurer’s Annual Report
  for Fiscal Year 2012-13 and Annual Review of the CDFA Investment Policy

  (1) Received and filed the CDFA Treasurer's Annual Report for Fiscal Year 2012-13; and
  (2) adopted CDFA Resolution 13-03 Approving the Authority's Investment Policy for FY
  2013-14.

11. Mission Viejo Housing Authority Treasurer’s Annual Report for Fiscal Year 2012-13
  and Annual Review of the Mission Viejo Housing Authority Investment Policy

  (1) Received and filed the MVHA Treasurer's Annual Report for Fiscal Year 2012-13; and
  (2) adopted Housing Authority Resolution 13-02 Approving the Mission Viejo Housing
  Authority Investment Policy for FY 2013-14.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

City Council Minutes  5  October 7, 2013
 OLD BUSINESS

NEW BUSINESS

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

2.  City Council Minutes

  Council Member Schlicht asked that reference to motorcycle officer monitoring of the
  crossing guard locations be added to the City Manager's comments on page 10 of the
  September 16, 2013, Minutes.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Leckness, to
  approve the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of September 16, 2013, as
  amended.

  AYES:  Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Kelley

3.  Check Register Dated September 6, 2013 in the Amount of $1,884,238.43

  Council Member Schlicht referred to page 4 of the report and asked why the City paid $630
  for security at the dog park.

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay responded that there had
  been some damage to the contractor's equipment and in order to keep the project moving
  along, the City posted a security guard at the site for 3 weekends while the heavy grading
  equipment was stored there.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ury, to ratify the
  accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Kelley

4.  Check Register Dated September 13, 2013 in the Amount of $309,529.48

  Council Member Schlicht inquired about a payment of $30,000 to Pacific Symphony for
  this year's concert and she noted that the previous donations were $20,000.

City Council Minutes  6  October 7, 2013
   Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay responded that all of the
  host cities were asked to donate $30,000 this year since Target's sponsorship has gone
  down. In fact, Target will no longer sponsor the Symphony events. Mr. Rattay stated that
  even with the larger donation, staff remained within the $58,000 budget for the event.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Leckness, to
  ratify the accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Kelley

5.  Check Register Dated September 20, 2013 in the Amount of $827,373.41

  Council Member Schlicht asked staff to provide an explanation for the purchase of
  furniture for the tennis center and for the dog park.

  Assistant City Manager/Director Rattay responded that the City purchased the dog park
  furniture however, the dog park fundraisers will offset the cost and he will bring an item
  before the Council on the next agenda to recognize the fundraiser revenue so it can be
  added to the CIP. Mr. Rattay noted that the Marguerite Tennis Center furniture was
  purchased to wrap up the renovation project before the City hosts the Wheelchair Tennis
  Masters in November.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Leckness, to
  ratify the accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Kelley

6.  Quarterly Check Registers and Quarterly Cash Receipts Report - Fourth Quarter of
  FY 2012-13

  Council Member Schlicht asked why corporate credit card purchasing has gone up and she
  stated that it would be a good idea to have an audit. She also requested a copy of the City's
  CAL Card policy manual, how many cards there are, a list of employees who have been
  issued a card and whether or not there are annual spending limits.

City Council Minutes  7  October 7, 2013
   Director Dyas confirmed that she will return at the next Council Meeting to provide a
  summary of the CAL Card program.

  Motion made by Mayor Reardon, seconded by Council Member Ury, to receive and file.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Kelley

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

12. Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Due to Mayor Pro Tem Kelley's absence, the report was delayed to the next City Council
  Meeting.

13. Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Reardon announced that there has not been a recent meeting of the Foothill/Eastern
  TCA.

14. San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Reardon announced that there has not been a recent meeting of the San Joaquin
  Hills TCA.

15. Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA)

  Council Member Ury presented the report.

16. SCAG Transportation & Communications Committee (TCC) Report

  With Mayor Pro Tem Kelley absent, the report was continued to the next City Council
  Meeting.

17. Orange County Vector Control District

  Council Member Leckness presented the report.

City Council Minutes  8  October 7, 2013
 18. Investment Advisory Commission Vacancy

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Reardon, to appoint Scot Shier
  to the Investment Advisory Commission.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Kelley

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report

19. Report on Recent Actions of the Successor Agency Oversight Board

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas provided a report on the recent meeting of
  the Successor Agency Oversight Board.

20. Close Out of FY 2012-13 and FY 2013-14 Budget Adjustments

  City Manager Wilberg presented an overview and Director Dyas presented the details of
  the FY 2012-13 close out and FY 2013-14 budget adjustments.

  Larry Gilbert, M.V.: presented the Council with a column that he wrote for the Common
  Sense newspaper in which he expresses his opposition the expenditure of over $1 million
  for a dog park.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Leckness, to (1)
  adopted Resolution 13-55 Amending the FY 2012-13 City Budget for Year-End Close Out
  Adjustments in Certain Accounts and Funds; and (2) adopted Resolution 13-56 Amending
  the FY 2013-14 City Budget, as amended.

  Amendment: directed staff to delete sections 2 and 3 from the Resolution which relate to
  the dog park.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Kelley

City Council Minutes  9  October 7, 2013
 City Attorney’s Report

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that he will bring back the modified multiple calls party
ordinance at the next City Council Meeting. If possible, he will send the Council Members an
advanced copy so they can provide input or ask questions ahead of the meeting.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

21. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as presented
  in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.

Council Member Leckness

Council Member Leckness announced that he attended Carden Academy's 20th anniversary
celebration and the Annual State of the College breakfast at Saddleback College. He outlined the
impressive transfer rate for Saddleback students to other colleges and universities and he noted
that President Todd Burnett is doing a great job and we are lucky to have such a gem in the
City. He also discussed the recent Secrets to Business Success Overseas seminar where
attendees learned about exporting products and services to China. Council Member Leckness
stated that Chinese consumers are willing to pay more for American products because they
believe the goods and services are high-quality and safe. He also attended the opening of the
Capistrano Valley High School Theater where the audience was entertained by vignettes of
different well-known plays. Lastly, Council Member Leckness announced that 650 people have
signed up for the annual Campout on October 19. He reminded residents that all they need is a
tent, a sleeping bag and a pillow and the City will provide food, entertainment, restrooms and
security. He stated that the location on the Oso Creek Trail is the greatest spot for a campout and
he invited everyone to join in the fun.

Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht announced that she recently attended a Saddleback Republican
Assembly meeting with guest speaker Brad Dacus. Mr. Dacus is President of an organization
that defends civil liberties and religious freedoms, at no cost. He has a network of attorneys
across the nation and one of his board members is Edwin Meese. Council Member Schlicht
announced that Southern California Gas Company will be conducting a test of gas lines and will
try to do so without interfering with service. She asked Assistant City Manager Rattay to let
everyone know what that's all about at the conclusion of tonight's meeting. She also outlined her
attendance at the NRC meeting on September 26 in Carlsbad. She stated that it was somewhat of
a dog and pony show because speakers were selected by the host so not everyone who wanted to
speak had the opportunity. She learned that there is $4 billion in the trust fund to decommission
San Onofre and it could take up to 60 years to do so. There is a big concern about what to do
with the buildup of hazardous waste not only at San Onofre, but at nuclear facilities across the
nation. Council Member Schlicht noted that there was a CPUC meeting in San Diego regarding
City Council Minutes  10  October 7, 2013
 SONGS where both the CPUC and the attendees agreed that SCE should be held responsible for
the cost of their mistakes at SONGS and hopefully the rate payers will receive refunds. She
announced that the next meeting regarding SONGS will be a symposium on October 19 from
1:30 to 4:30 p.m. at the Center for Spiritual Living in San Clemente, 1201 Puerto del Sol, 1st
floor. Council Member Schlicht quoted Thomas Jefferson: "A government big enough to give
you everything you want is big enough to take away everything you have," and lastly, she
discussed her attendance at recent Diablos football games and she encouraged everyone to get
out and support local schools and their teams.

Council Member Ury

Council Member Ury announced that the Orange County Transportation Authority held an open
house at the Murray Center to discuss the 405 widening project. The attendees heard a lot of
good information and there will be other public meetings on the same subject. He also had the
opportunity to discuss the 405 widening project on the early morning cable access television
show in Laguna Woods and he noted that the goal at OCTA is to accelerate the project. Lastly,
Council Member Ury thanked staff, especially Jerry Hill and his team, for helping his son Alex
with his Eagle Scout project.

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley was absent

Mayor Reardon

Mayor Reardon highlighted her attendance at the annual Saddleback College State of the College
breakfast and she praised President Burnett for the great job he does and for backing up his
statements with documentation. The college has over 40,000 students and they are very broad in
meeting the needs of the community. She noted that Saddleback has one of the best nursing
programs in the country and they expedite and assist students with a smooth transition to Cal
State Fullerton, among other colleges and universities. Mayor Reardon said that she enjoyed
speaking to a local Boy Scout troop on the workings of local government and she always looks
forward to the Scouts' questions. She also visited Carl Hankey School which has an
International Baccalaureate (IB) program. The school’s Principal and a teacher will highlight the
IB program at an upcoming City Council Meeting. Mayor Reardon outlined her attendance at
recent events including a Nuclear Regulatory Commission meeting on San Onofre, the South
Orange County Economic Coalition meeting where the subject was Obamacare, and the Rancho
Santa Margarita State of the City event. She also had the opportunity to read to 70 kindergarten
students at Del Lago Elementary and she attended the Orange County Automobile Dealers
Association luncheon with guest speaker Marcus Luttrelle, author of Lone Survivor. Mr.
Luttrelle was the only survivor of Operation Redwing and his book chronicles the heroism of the
navy seals who died in the attack in Afghanistan. Mayor Reardon outlined upcoming events
including Heart to Heart, a symposium for parents and teens about the prescription drug abuse
epidemic, on October 9 from 7:00 to 9:00 p.m. at the Murray Community Center; the Walk
Against Drugs and Emergency Preparedness Fair on October 19; the annual Camp Out event on
October 19; the screening of the movie Bully in the Council Chamber on October 20 beginning
City Council Minutes  11  October 7, 2013
 at 2:00 p.m.; and a Solar Decathlon from October 10 through 13 at the Great Park in
Irvine. Mayor Reardon noted that her friends watched the last Council Meeting on television
and were confused by Council Member Schlicht's comments about the June 3 Minutes and an
alleged Brown Act violation. She noted that she would ordinarily let this pass however Council
Member Schlicht could have corrected the record by clarifying the statements in question at a
subsequent meeting. Instead, she asserted that the City Clerk politically wrote the Minutes and
that there was a Brown Act violation via an email exchange. Mayor Reardon stated that Karen
Hamman is probably the most apolitical person in the building. She believes that Karen is
unbiased and takes painstaking care to document only what has been said and she does not
record inference. Mayor Reardon noted that the Council had approved the June 3 Minutes on
June17 as written, pending the City Clerk's review of Council Member Schlicht's comments on
the video recording. Council Member Ury had given Council Member Schlicht some feedback
and that would have been the ideal time for Council Member Schlicht to correct her
statements. There was an email exchange on June 18 and City Attorney Curley advised the
Council on the Brown Act and how to avoid any issues. Mr. Curley, who is an expert in the
Brown Act, has confirmed that there was no violation and Mayor Reardon announced that she
brought this up in order to correct the record on the matter.

Responding to Council Member Schlicht's earlier request, Assistant City Manager/Director of
Administrative Services Keith Rattay announced that Southern California Gas Company will be
conducting tests on a high pressure natural gas line that goes through the City of Mission
Viejo. They expect that there will be no impact on service to the community.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 8:15 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Reardon adjourned the meeting to Monday, October 21, 2013, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of October 21, 2013

City Council Minutes  12  October 7, 2013
